subject.title: [Bug]: Embedded runner "Network connection lost" when LLM generates a tool call with large parameters (param generation latency > underlying request timeout)

question: Should OpenClaw treat OpenRouter-routed Anthropic large tool-call argument generation as a default reliability guarantee, or leave it as an operator-tuned provider timeout workaround?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the durable fix changes provider timeout and streaming semantics where defaults affect cost, failover, and stuck-provider detection.

options.title: Live-prove provider-owned fix
options.body: Reproduce the issue with OpenRouter Anthropic, then implement the narrowest OpenRouter/provider-stream or timeout policy change with before/after proof.

options.title: Document timeout workaround only
options.body: Keep current behavior and improve docs around `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds`, accepting that users must tune slow large-argument generations themselves.

options.title: Raise cloud watchdog defaults
options.body: Increase default cloud first-event or idle timeouts globally, accepting slower detection of genuinely stuck provider calls.

recommendation.title: Live-prove provider-owned fix
recommendation.body: Reproduce the issue with OpenRouter Anthropic, then implement the narrowest OpenRouter/provider-stream or timeout policy change with before/after proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans embedded-runner timeout policy and provider failure semantics, where recent history points most strongly to this runtime area owner.
